title: Microwindow prefetch scheduler for hybrid prompt/response workloads
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Problem statement: mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts + long responses, and vice versa) lead to two related production issues: 1) KV cache fragmentation where long-running responses pin large KV slabs and prevent efficient coalescing of short requests, increasing GPU memory pressure; 2) tail-latency spikes caused by poor slot packing and late prefetches when interactive short-turn dialog requests arrive concurrently with streaming long generations. Current continuous batcher groups by arrival time and length buckets, but we see suboptimal residency and expensive background GC during peak traffic.

Goal: design and implement a scheduler variant that reduces GPU memory footprint and p95/p99 latency for mixed-length traffic by (a) prefetching and reserving microwindows of KV for expected short bursts, (b) proactively compacting/evicting cold KV using a temporal-decay residency score, and (c) allowing limited cross-dialog prefix coalescing when safe for routing policies. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation behind a feature flag, and end-to-end perf validation in the staging cluster.
acceptance_criteria: Feature gated behind 'microwindow_prefetch' flag and off by default
Prefetch scheduler must not increase median latency by >5% for baseline workloads
p95 latency improvement >= 10% for mixed prompt/response synthetic benchmark (see bench-2026-03-08)
Net GPU memory usage reduction >= 12% under mixed dialog workload compared to current continuous batcher
No request-level correctness regressions (chat history fidelity, KV lookups) — automated regression tests pass
Operational metrics published to Console: kv_residency_score, microwindow_evictions, microwindow_prefetch_ratio, slot_coalesce_rate
implementation_notes: Scheduler overview: on admit, compute an expected 'microwindow' size for the request using EWMA of recent sequence lengths per user/session and global percentile windows. For short-adjacent arrivals, attempt to coalesce into an existing microwindow slot rather than a full-length slot.

KV residency score: compute score = alpha * recency_rank + beta * (token_residency_bytes / slot_capacity) + gamma * prefix_hotness. Use exponential decay (half-life configurable) to age out old prefixes and make eviction decisions low-latency-friendly.

Prefetch path: when admitting a request predicted to start a long response, prefetch KV into an ephemeral microwindow with relaxed pinning (low-residency priority). If the response grows beyond the microwindow, escalate to a full slot with copy-on-write semantics to avoid double-reading the model.
Compaction: background compactor scans low-residency microwindows and performs KV coalescing at off-peak times. Must be rate-limited by GPU bandwidth and avoid impacting active slot throughput.

Routing and safety: cross-dialog prefix coalescing allowed only when the routing policy is 'trusted' and request-level privacy flags are absent. For customer-owned Private deployments, default is conservative (no cross-dialog coalescing) unless tenant opts-in.
Metrics and tracing: add histograms for eviction latency and counters for escalation events. Tag traces with 'microwindow=true/false' to compare paths in Flamegraphs.
Feature flag & rollout: implement server-side flag 'microwindow_prefetch_v1'. Start with 5% traffic in staging, then ramp in canary across dedicated nodes before wider rollout.
Backwards compat: ensure model kernel selection and kv-format invariants are preserved; no changes to on-disk KV encodings in this phase.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Initial design doc posted (link above). Reviewed with serving-runtime and infra teams. Key feedback: keep prefetch bandwidth budgeted and prefer eviction over blocking allocations.
2026-03-04: Prototype microwindow admit logic implemented in the adaptive-batcher module behind flag. Unit tests added for microwindow sizing heuristics.

2026-03-06: First staging run with synthetic mixed-length traffic (80% short prompts 10-50 tokens, 20% long responses 800-2k tokens). Observed 14% reduction in peak GPU resident bytes on node type g4dn-like. p95 improved ~9% (below target) — investigating prefetch delay tuning.
2026-03-08: Tuned EWMA half-life and prefetch lead time; re-run bench-2026-03-08 saw p95 improvement 12% and p99 down 18%. Collected allocation flamegraphs for follow-up.
2026-03-09: Design review with security/compliance: confirmed default conservative policy for Private deployments. Added explicit opt-in in config schema for cross-dialog coalescing.
2026-03-10: Implemented background compactor rate-limiter and added metrics. Preparing canary plan and PR (see comments).
comments: Markus Li (2026-03-03): Prototype looks good — watch out for bursty short traffic where prefetch could waste bandwidth. Suggest bounded prefetch tokens per node.
Priya Banerjee (Infra, 2026-03-05): Need to ensure compaction doesn't contend with NVLink copies; set compaction QPS based on node-level GPU utilization.
Dmitri Orlov (PM, 2026-03-07): Add a Console dashboard tile comparing microwindow vs baseline for sample tenants; product wants to see cost-per-1M tokens delta.
Security (2026-03-09): Approved conservative defaults; require explicit admin consent for cross-dialog coalescing in tenant settings.
next_steps: Merge PR for feature flag and instrumentation: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1128
Canary 5% traffic run on dedicated nodes (planner: 2026-03-12) and capture longsessions vs shortsessions traces
If canary metrics match acceptance criteria, incrementally ramp to 25% then 50% with rollback conditions defined
Run cost analysis for hosted API customers to quantify per-token unit savings and decide if we expose tuning controls in Console
